title: Runtime salvage for GPU OOM cascade caused by KV-index drift and slab spiral
creator: Jordan Kim
summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private observed GPU OOM cascades during long-lived sessions and high-concurrency bursts. Investigation shows a KV index desynchronization that prevents tombstone reclamation and amplifies slab fragmentation; the allocator then rejects new allocations under heavy KV churn leading to OOMs. This ticket tracks the runtime patch, rollout, and short/medium-term mitigations.
impact_details: Incidents started on 2025-11-02 with a hosted customer (multi-tenant) reporting repeated 503s and node evictions. Dedicated pools with prolonged context workloads then exhibited degraded capacity after 48–72h. Private installs surfaced the same defect on two air-gapped clusters after sustained session churn. Affected customers: 3 hosted customers with production traffic, 2 mid-market dedicated tenants, and 2 Private deployments in evaluation.
root_cause_summary: A race in KV index reconciliation when spillover compaction runs concurrently with slot reclamation caused stale index entries (ghost slots). The allocator's slab accounting didn't decrement correctly for those ghost slots, leaving fragmented free ranges that the per-GPU allocator couldn't coalesce under heavy allocation patterns. Long-lived sessions with intermittent caching and aggressive evictions amplified fragmentation until new allocations hit OOM thresholds. Secondary contributor: the compaction trigger thresholds were too conservative in high-churn workloads, delaying reclamation.
technical_action_plan: 1) Runtime patch: make index reconciliation atomic by introducing a per-shard reconciliation lock and fix slot reference counting to ensure decrement on spill and tombstone apply. 2) Allocator change: add a background micro-compactor that coalesces adjacent freed slab runs (configurable window) and exposes a diagnostic metric. 3) Safety: short-circuit large single-request allocations to fallback model variants when free contiguous slab cannot be found. 4) Tests: add deterministic fuzz tests for concurrent spill+reconcile and two new stress benchmarks that simulate long session churn.
short_term_mitigations:
- Throttle session creation on impacted pools (automated via autoscaler hook).
- Increase compaction aggressiveness for affected pools (runtime flag).
- Rolling restarts for most-fragmented nodes to reclaim ephemeral arenas as emergency relief.
- Customer comms: notify affected tenants with recommended temporary SDK backoff and reduction of max-concurrent sessions.
canary_and_rollout_plan: 1) Canary: deploy runtime-1.21.1 with the KV-index atomic patch to a single hosted-region pool with low-util non-critical traffic for 12h. 2) Metrics to watch: GPU OOM count, slab-fragmentation_ratio, kvcache_tombstone_count, allocation_failures, tail latency. 3) If stable, expand to remaining hosted pools over 24h with staggered ramp. 4) Apply to Dedicated pools next (rolling window by customer and risk), notifying tenants 6h prior. 5) Private deployments: provide patch bundle and operator instructions; offer assisted upgrade for high-risk customers.
rollback_plan: Revert to previous runtime binary on per-pool basis using existing orchestration. If allocator regressions appear (unexpected latency or allocation failure spikes), flip "micro_compactor.enabled" to false and pause rollout. Detailed rollback playbook is in the linked incident runbook.
validation_criteria:
- Zero GPU OOM regressions attributable to KV index races in canary window.
- kvcache_tombstone_count reduces to baseline within 2 compaction windows.
- slab_fragmentation_ratio drops by >=30% on previously fragmented nodes.
- No increase in tail latency >5% in 95/99th percentile across canary traffic.
postmortem_actions:
- Add long-running session churn workload to CI stress suite.
- Ship allocator diagnostics (per-slab free-range histograms) to Console for long-term monitoring.
- Rework compaction thresholds and expose knob in Console for Dedicated customers.
- Run a targeted audit of other reconciliation paths for similar races.

- Internal Slack channel #inc-runtime-kv created for coordination.
